---
title: "Contributing"
description: "How to fix a page or add a new tutorial to this site."
---

This site is written by people in the lab, for people in the lab. If you spot a mistake, or you've worked out how to do something that others would find useful, please add it.

You don't need to install anything to contribute. Everything below can be done in your web browser on GitHub. All you need is a [GitHub account](https://github.com/signup).

## How it works

Every page on this site is a plain text file in the [PiNC-lab/PiNC-lab.github.io](https://github.com/PiNC-lab/PiNC-lab.github.io) repository on GitHub. When someone changes one of those files, the website rebuilds itself a few minutes later.

You can't change the lab's copy of the files directly. Instead you:

1. Make your own copy of the repository (a **fork**).
2. Make your change in your copy.
3. Ask for your change to be brought into the lab's copy (a **pull request**).

Someone who looks after the site checks the change and merges it. GitHub walks you through most of this, as described below.

If forks and pull requests are new to you, the [Git and GitHub tutorial](tutorials/git-github.qmd#the-lab-organisation-forks-and-pull-requests) explains them in more detail. You don't need to read it first.

## Fix or improve an existing page

This is the quickest way to correct a typo, update a link or add a few lines.

1. On the page you want to change, click **Edit this page** on the right-hand side (under the table of contents) or at the bottom of the page.
2. GitHub opens the file. If it says you need to fork the repository to propose changes, click **Fork this repository**.
3. Make your change in the editor. Use the **Preview** tab to check how it looks.
4. Click **Commit changes...**. Write a short note saying what you changed, for example "Fix broken link to Zenodo", and click **Propose changes**.
5. On the next page, click **Create pull request**, then **Create pull request** again.

That's it. You'll get an email when someone has looked at it. If they ask for a change, make it the same way, and it gets added to the same pull request.

## Add a new tutorial or how-to

Tutorials live in the `tutorials` folder. Each one is a single `.qmd` file, which is Markdown with a short header at the top.

1. Go to the [repository](https://github.com/PiNC-lab/PiNC-lab.github.io) and click **Fork** at the top right, then **Create fork**. You now have your own copy at `github.com/your-username/PiNC-lab.github.io`. (If you've forked it before, open your fork and click **Sync fork** first so it's up to date.)
2. In your fork, open the `tutorials` folder and then [`_template.qmd`](https://github.com/PiNC-lab/PiNC-lab.github.io/blob/main/tutorials/_template.qmd). Click the **Raw** button and copy all the text.
3. Go back to the `tutorials` folder, click **Add file > Create new file**, and name it something short with dashes instead of spaces, ending in `.qmd`, for example `camera-trap-data.qmd`.
4. Paste in the template and replace the text with your own. Fill in the `title`, `description`, `categories`, `date` and `author` lines at the top; the home page uses these.
5. Click **Commit changes...**. Choose **Create a new branch for this commit**, give it a name like `add-camera-trap-tutorial`, and click **Propose changes**.
6. Check that the top of the page says you're asking to merge into `PiNC-lab/PiNC-lab.github.io` on `main`, write a sentence or two about what you've added, and click **Create pull request**.

### Adding pictures

Put image files in the `tutorials/images` folder. In your fork, open that folder, click **Add file > Upload files**, drag the files in, and commit them to the same branch as your tutorial. Then link to them in your tutorial:

```markdown
![Camera trap set up on a fence post](images/camera-trap-setup.jpg)
```

Keep images small (under 1 MB if you can). Screenshots and photos straight off a phone are often much larger than they need to be.

## Writing pages

Pages are written in Markdown. The essentials:

| You write | You get |
|---|---|
| `## Section heading` | A section heading (it appears in the table of contents) |
| `**bold**` and `*italic*` | **bold** and *italic* |
| `[link text](https://example.com)` | [link text](https://example.com) |
| `- item` on separate lines | A bulleted list |
| `1. step` on separate lines | A numbered list |
| `` `install.packages("terra")` `` | `install.packages("terra")` |

For a block of code, put three backticks and the language on the line before, and three backticks on the line after:

````markdown
```r
library(terra)
r <- rast("elevation.tif")
```
````

Code on this site is shown, not run, so you don't need any data or packages for the page to build. The [Quarto Markdown guide](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html) covers everything else, including tables, footnotes and callout boxes.

A few tips:

- Write for someone in the lab a year from now who wasn't in the room. Say what they need installed and where any data come from.
- Short sections with clear headings are easier to follow than long ones.
- Don't include passwords, API keys, or personal or sensitive data. Everything in this repository is public.

## What happens after you open a pull request

- GitHub automatically checks that the site still builds with your change. A green tick means it's fine. A red cross means something went wrong; click **Details** to see what, or just ask for help in the pull request.
- Someone who looks after the site reads it, and either merges it or leaves a comment.
- Once it's merged, the live site updates within a few minutes.

## Working on your own computer (optional)

For bigger changes, such as a long tutorial with lots of images, you may prefer to work in RStudio. RStudio comes with Quarto built in.

1. Fork the repository and clone your fork in RStudio (**File > New Project > Version Control > Git**). The [Git and GitHub tutorial](tutorials/git-github.qmd) explains each of these steps.
2. Make a branch for your change: `git switch -c add-my-tutorial`.
3. Add or edit files. To see the whole site as it will look, run this in the RStudio **Terminal**:

   ```bash
   quarto preview
   ```

4. Commit, push to your fork with `git push -u origin add-my-tutorial`, and open a pull request on GitHub.

## Suggest something without writing it

If you'd like a tutorial on something but don't want to write it, or you've found a problem you can't fix yourself, click **Report an issue** on any page, or [open an issue](https://github.com/PiNC-lab/PiNC-lab.github.io/issues/new) on the repository and describe it.
